notes:
Arizona has no recurring franchise-type levy on a default LLC: applies is false. The only corporate-level filing the collector describes for an LLC is the corporate income tax return an LLC must file after electing to be taxed as a corporation; a default partnership-taxed LLC is outside it. The Department's own businesses index enumerates the taxes Arizona administers (corporate income, transaction privilege, withholding, property, and the excises) and names no franchise tax.
The transaction privilege tax (TPT) is excluded rather than recorded as the franchise levy, and the call is in this note. TPT is a tax on a vendor for the privilege of doing business, but it is a transaction tax: A.R.S. 42-5008 levies privilege taxes 'measured by the amount or volume of business transacted by persons on account of their business activities', applied through business classifications (retail, restaurants, lodging, etc.) and accompanied by a use tax; an existing LLC with no TPT-classified activity owes nothing and files nothing, and the $12 license is a registration fee. The Ohio/Washington/Oregon gross-receipts privilege taxes recorded elsewhere in this namespace reach nearly every business with receipts above a threshold; TPT reaches only enumerated transactions, so recording it here would overstate what a default LLC owes for existing. An active LLC engaged in a TPT-classified activity must register, collect, and remit TPT like any other vendor - that is an activity obligation, not an existence levy.
collectedWithAnnualReport is null: no franchise-type levy exists, and root states.json carries annual_report_fee 0 for Arizona because LLCs are not required to file annual reports (the Secretary of State's requirement is corporations-only).
stateIncomeTax: members owe Arizona individual income tax on their pass-through shares. A.R.S. 43-1011(A)(9) sets a flat 2.5% rate for taxable years beginning after the year the Department of Revenue provides the notice described in 43-243(B)(2); the Department's Pub 713 (November 2025) confirms the rate by stating the 2025 Pass-Through Entity income tax is assessed at 2.50%. Arizona offers the elective Pass-Through Entity tax under A.R.S. 43-1011's pass-through entity provisions: a partnership (including a partnership-taxed LLC) or S corporation may elect to have flow-through income taxed at the entity level at 2.50%, and owners claim the corresponding credit. The election is made on Form 165 (partnerships, which is the default LLC's form) or Form 120S.
